summary: The app's own native sketch solver can now solve drag targets, ahead of answering drags in the app; drags are still solved by PlaneGCS. A drag target is a temporary value relation on a dragged coordinate. The native solver keeps every lasting relation met and moves the dragged values toward their targets: onto them when reachable, within max(1e-8, 32 epsilon S) mm and exactly where the lasting relations still accept that, otherwise to values on the start's branch where it finds nothing closer, such as the nearest point of a circle or the end of a stretched arm. Each step is a damped tangent step toward the targets, sized to a trust radius and restored onto the lasting relations, with a line search on the restored path's slopes that also lengthens the next step where the path curves less than the step assumed, as near a far target or off the far side of a circle. Motion below a few ulps of the targeted coordinates does not count as progress. A drag is reported projected when the first- and second-order necessary conditions of a nearest point hold up to the solver's resolution; that does not prove the point nearest, and higher orders are not checked. The projected gradient must be small. The multipliers come from a factor of the transposed Jacobian damped only at the Jacobian's own roundoff; a verified bound on that factor's inverse, from its comparison matrix or a verified Frobenius norm, bounds the smallest singular value from below, and with it each curved relation's multiplier error, so large multipliers on unrelated relations do not hide it. A curved relation whose multiplier is within that error, plus the change the first-order tolerance allows, of zero counts as carrying none. The directions the relations leave free come from the singular values of the null-space projector's columns on the targeted and curved coordinates, with a bounded error: a free direction whose share of support motion is between twice and eight times that error is not resolved, and one within twice its error, about 1e-12 for a well-conditioned group, counts as held. The curvature of the target distance along the free directions, per unit of support motion and with row Hessians from central differences of the exact gradients, must not be negative beyond its error, about 1e-10 of the relations' weighted curvature. The test is of a relaxation: collapsed distances and relations the factor finds dependent are left out, and the remaining relations must still explain the gradient. Within these limits a construction geared about 2^20 into a weak multiplier, or 2^40 into a direction that looks held, can be reported projected at a point that is not nearest; PlaneGCS stops at such points too. A curvature is taken as negative only beyond what the kept relations' errors, the relations counted as carrying none and roundoff could bend it back along that direction. A clearly negative curvature, as at the far side of a circle or a straight arm with a target inside its reach, is followed by restored steps of halving length. A curvature within its error of zero is followed at two restored trial lengths along the flat direction that moves the targets most; when neither gains, the drag is projected, with higher orders not checked. Every other case reports the drag stalled at its last feasible values: multipliers or free directions too weakly determined to bound, a collapsed or dependent relation the rest cannot replace, or a test spanning more than 64 columns. A start that cannot be restored onto the lasting relations, including a group with only fixed values whose relations fail, is reported stalled, with the group not converged. A landing on the targets stands only when every target of the group is then within reach and the lasting relations accept it, and polishes the rest of its group; a polish cut short, including one that ends accepted after its work ran out, leaves the landing as it was. Restoring the start, the trials and the landing share one budget of 400 iterations per group, and a check the budget cuts short decides nothing; the drag charges each solve before running it, and the curvature test also its ordering, its reduced curvature matrix and its dense eigensolves; work running out is reported as too large. Groups without drag targets keep their values when those already meet their relations, and are otherwise solved as without a drag. The solver reports whether the targets were reached, projected or stalled, and the remaining target distance, in protocol 3 of its buffer format; the group status reflects the lasting relations, so a stalled drag at feasible values still reports converged. Solves without drag targets return the same results bit for bit as 0.0.746.
warning: No breaking change for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions, CAD files or controller output, and no change to what the app shows: drags are still answered by PlaneGCS until a later release routes them to the native solver. The native solver's buffer format moves to protocol 3, which the app's bundled module and reader share.

checklist.schema: No UPID, post, machine package, execution plan, saved revision, CAD, storage, journal or worker reply schema change. The native solver buffer protocol moves from 2 to 3: two header fields for the drag outcome and target distance, and temporary relations accepted only as value relations. Post engine API remains 1 and saved-job engine remains 3.
checklist.events: No execution event, cancellation or input-version behavior change. WebMCP tools keep their arguments and results.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change and no new application controls.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change.
checklist.verification: Rust drag tests cover a free point landing exactly on its target; a point on a circle reaching the nearest point to far targets (15, 100 and 1e6 mm away) and leaving the far side of its circle; a target at the circle's centre, where every point is equally near, projected on its circle; circle drags independent of position (offsets 1e6 and -3e8 mm) and scale (1e-3 to 1e3); the foot of a target on a line; far targets beside a linear relation and a short guide; fixed and held coordinates counted in the distance but kept; groups without targets kept exactly; an elbow keeping its side; an infeasible start that stalls; exhausted work reported as too large and feasible; identical bits for the same drag, with an out-of-reach two-link arm stretched toward its target; only value relations accepted as targets; a landing polishing the rest of its group; a straight arm folding toward a target inside its reach and staying straight toward one beyond it; a 0.001 mm circle leaving its far side for a target 1e9 mm away, and for a near target with the circle 3e8 mm from the origin; straight two-link arms in any direction and a folded-back three-link chain reaching targets inside their reach; a point on a line it can also turn leaving a start that neither motion alone improves; a stretched chain of 30 joints projected and one of 40 reported stalled past the curvature test's support; a repeated distance relation still projected; a point flat to second order whose distance falls at fourth order leaving its start; a collapsed distance never projected, also beside a large multiplier from an unrelated far target; a weakly determined circle multiplier beside multipliers near 1e12 from an unrelated far drag not projected; a distance or radius between two fixed points treated as linear; a landing polish that runs out of work, at any allowance from 150 to 1000, leaving the landing as it was and otherwise matching the full polish; a point at the far side of its circle with a chain of 18 doublings hanging off it, whose free direction barely moves the point, leaving the far side and never projected short of the nearest point, and one with 20 doublings not projected at the far side; a unit circle geared by 10 doublings into a 1e6 mm circle, which bends only 1e-6 per mm, leaving its start; a line collinear with a fixed line, dragged off it with its other end free, projected; that line tied to the fourth-order point, whose flat set holds both the free slide and a target-moving turn, never projected at the start; a far-side point geared 2^17 into a circle whose multiplier is too weak to count but whose bend outweighs the antipode's, projected there rather than escaping; a far-side point 1e8 mm from the origin geared 2^12 into a unit circle, whose bends nearly cancel within the differencing error, not taken for a maximum; two targets 7e-9 mm either side of one free value reached at zero rather than landed on either; a group of only fixed values whose relation fails reported stalled and not converged; eight tied circles whose curvature test's eigensolves, and 100 repeated circles whose ordering, run out of work reported too large, as do 63 circles sharing one coordinate whose reduced curvature matrix does; a 100-link chain whose curvature test runs out of work reported too large; a slight negative curvature (1e-6 per mm on a 1000 mm circle) followed; a far out-of-reach drag staying within the iteration budget; and a point leaving the farthest point of its circle for the nearest within half the iteration budget. Unit tests cover the transposed triangular solve, the Jacobi eigensolver and small singular values keeping their absolute accuracy. The reader tests cover protocol 3 replies with and without a drag outcome and reject an unknown outcome, a missing, partial or invalid distance, drag fields missing for a model with drag targets, and an outcome for a model without them. Every non-drag native solve in the native-differential suites and the CAD browser and pure-domain suites (3240 solves) was compared bit for bit with the 0.0.746 module, without a difference. On the die and the free die, dragging each point 0.58 mm and 47 mm (188 drags), the native solver never ended further from its target than PlaneGCS, reached or projected every one (166 projected, 22 reached, none stalled) within 78 iterations, and answered the 164 drags PlaneGCS solved in 238 ms of module calls against 405 ms of PlaneGCS solves; held points settle in one iteration. It was slower only for one chamfer point dragged far (7.1 ms against 5.2 ms). The module grows from 92 to 180 kB.

changes: Teaches the app's own sketch solver to follow drags, ahead of using it for dragging in a later release.
